package_info.why_malicious: The package exploits NuGet's autorun mechanism by embedding a malicious install.ps1 script that executes automatically upon installation. This script sets the PowerShell execution policy to Unrestricted, downloads an executable from a hardcoded remote IP address, saves it to the user's APPDATA directory, and immediately executes it. This behavior is highly atypical for legitimate NuGet packages and is used to deliver second-stage malware, such as crypto stealers and persistence updaters.

execution_context.trigger: During package installation via NuGet's autorun mechanism (init.ps1/install.ps1)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During package installation via NuGet's autorun script, the code sets the PowerShell execution policy to Unrestricted, downloads an executable from a hardcoded remote IP address, writes the file to the user's %APPDATA% directory, and immediately executes the downloaded binary, resulting in the launch of a second-stage payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script modifies the PowerShell execution policy to Unrestricted, which disables script execution protections, then downloads and executes a remote binary from a hardcoded IP address without user consent. This is a classic malware dropper pattern and is never expected in legitimate package installation scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate NuGet packages should not alter system execution policies, download executables from untrusted remote sources, or execute binaries during installation. Such actions violate the principle of least privilege and user trust.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: In rare cases, internal enterprise packages may bootstrap trusted tools, but they would not fetch executables from untrusted IPs or set execution policy to Unrestricted. Legitimate use would always involve signed binaries and trusted internal sources.
key_indicators: Modifies PowerShell execution policy to Unrestricted in the registry
Downloads executable from hardcoded external IP address (http://194.233.93.50/Avalon.exe)
Executes the downloaded binary immediately after download
Script is triggered automatically during package installation

execution_context.trigger: During installation of a package that declares Sys.Forms.26 as a dependency

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the package declares a dependency on Sys.Forms.26, which causes NuGet to automatically install the malicious package and trigger its autorun script, resulting in the execution of the embedded PowerShell payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The dependency is on an obscure, unrelated package whose only purpose is to execute a malicious payload during installation. This is a common technique to propagate malware via dependency confusion or typosquatting.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Dependencies in .nuspec files should reference legitimate, functionally related libraries. Using dependencies solely to trigger code execution is a clear abuse of the package ecosystem.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages declare dependencies for required libraries or frameworks, not to execute code as a side effect. There is no valid reason for a package to depend on an unrelated, malicious package.
key_indicators: Obscure dependency with no functional justification
Dependency chain used to trigger malicious code execution
Dependency on a package known to contain autorun scripts

attack_chain.action: User installs a malicious or typosquatted NuGet package (e.g., Discord-RichPresence, Coinbase.Core, Asip.Net.Core, Avalon-Net-Core) that declares a dependency on Sys.Forms.26.
attack_chain.leads_to: Triggers installation of the malicious dependency.

attack_chain.action: NuGet installs the Sys.Forms.26 dependency, which contains an install.ps1 autorun script that executes automatically.
attack_chain.leads_to: Executes the embedded PowerShell dropper script.

attack_chain.action: The PowerShell script sets the execution policy to Unrestricted, downloads a remote executable from a hardcoded IP, writes it to %APPDATA%, and executes it.
attack_chain.leads_to: Second-stage payload (e.g., Avalon.exe) is executed on the victim's system.

attack_chain.action: The second-stage payload (Avalon.exe or similar) performs malicious actions such as credential and crypto wallet theft, exfiltration via Discord webhooks, and persistence via updater components.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive data and maintains persistence on the victim's system.

behavioral_signatures: NuGet package installation triggers execution of install.ps1 or init.ps1 scripts
PowerShell script modifies execution policy to Unrestricted during package installation
PowerShell script downloads and executes binaries from hardcoded external IP addresses
Autorun scripts present in tools/install.ps1 or tools/init.ps1 within NuGet packages
Immediate process creation of new executables in user profile directories following package installation
file_indicators: Presence of tools/install.ps1 or tools/init.ps1 in NuGet package contents
Downloaded executable named Avalon.exe (or similar) in %APPDATA% directory
Suspicious dependency declarations in .nuspec files (e.g., dependency on Sys.Forms.26)
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to hardcoded IPs (e.g., 194.233.93.50, 62.182.84.61, 195.58.39.167)
Access to paste sites for payload retrieval (e.g., https://paste.bingner.com/paste/xden6/raw)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor NuGet package installations for the presence and execution of autorun scripts (install.ps1/init.ps1) that modify execution policy, download remote executables, or initiate outbound network connections. Flag packages with suspicious or unrelated dependencies, especially those matching known malicious names (e.g., Sys.Forms.26). Detect and alert on outbound HTTP requests to known C2 IPs and Discord webhooks, as well as the creation and execution of new binaries in user profile directories immediately after package installation. Monitor registry changes to PowerShell execution policy as an additional indicator.
